title: Generic failure of fibre-assassin containment persists on a nonempty base open
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], and let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume that $|Y|$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] and let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. For $y\in Y$, use the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ and the tensor pullback $F_y$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; associated points are [def-trf-relative-assassin]. If $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_\eta}(F_\eta)\not\subseteq |U_\eta|$, there exists a nonempty open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in |V|$ one has $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(F_y)\not\subseteq |U_y|$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ and no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $U$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose $\xi_\eta\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_\eta}(F_\eta)\setminus U_\eta$ and let $\xi\in X$ be its image. By [def-trf-relative-assassin], $\xi\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/Y}(F)$ and $f(\xi)=\eta$. Also $\xi\notin U$, since $U_\eta$ is the inverse image of $U$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\eta$ and an affine chart $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ in the finite-type affine cover of $f^{-1}(Y_0)$ containing $\xi$, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra. Restrict $F$ and $U$ to $X_0$. The local rings and module stalks on each fibre at points of $X_0$ are unchanged by open restriction, so the associated-point condition is unchanged by its stalk definition. It suffices to produce the required open in $Y_0$: it is also open in $Y$, with the same fibres and witnesses in $X$.

source.place: Tag 05F1, proof, affine-neighbourhood reduction; definitions of fibre and relative assassin.

proof.text: Let $Z=\overline{\{\xi\}}\subseteq X_0$ with its reduced closed structure, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Since $X_0\setminus U$ is closed and contains $\xi$, it contains $Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-assassin-neighbourhood] to $X_0\to Y_0$ and $F|_{X_0}$. Its hypotheses hold: this morphism is finite type, hence locally finite type; restriction preserves the local presentations expressing quasi-coherence and finite type of $F$. It gives a nonempty open $W\subseteq Z$ whose fibre component generic points map to associated points of $F_y|_{(X_0)_y}$. Since $Z$ is the closure of $\xi$, every nonempty open of $Z$ contains $\xi$. Choose a principal affine open $P\subseteq W$ containing $\xi$ in the affine scheme $Z$.

source.place: Tag 05F1, statement, applied to the bad associated point; reduced closed structure: Tag 01J3.

proof.text: We check the finite-type hypothesis needed to spread nonemptiness. By the affine clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ for a radical ideal $I$, and $P=\operatorname{Spec}((B/I)_g)$ for some $g\in B/I$. This is a finite type $A$-algebra: the images of finitely many generators of $B/A$, together with $g^{-1}$, generate it, with the sole extra localization relation $g g^{-1}=1$. Thus $P\to Y_0$ is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its generic fibre contains the point $\xi$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty] with total space $P$, base $Y_0$, and closed subset $C=|P|$. We obtain an open $V\subseteq Y_0$ containing $\eta$ for which $P_y$ is nonempty for every $y\in V$. The base has generic point $\eta$ because every nonempty open of the irreducible $Y$ contains it. No Noetherian, reducedness or separatedness assumption is needed by the cited node.

source.place: Tag 05F5 (lemma-nonempty-generic-fibre); existing generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty applied to the whole source.

proof.text: Fix $y\in V$. A point of $P_y\subseteq W_y$ lies in an irreducible component of $W_y$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] that component has a generic point $z$. Step 2 gives that its image in $(X_0)_y$ is associated to $F_y|_{(X_0)_y}$, and hence associated to $F_y$ by the identical-stalk observation of Step 1. That image is in $Z\subseteq X_0\setminus U$, so it lies outside $U_y$. We have obtained an associated point outside $U_y$ for every $y\in V$. As $\eta\in V$, this open is nonempty, proving the assertion.
